newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end firmer, Fiat jumps higher.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end firmer, Fiat jumps higher.

text.p: 1630 GMT - Milan shares ended higher helped by the firmer trend to bonds and Wall Street with trade union support for the government's Euro-tax seen as supportive, while Fiat shares jumped as the government considered help for the car industry.

* Italy's foreign trade minister Augusto Fantozzi said the government is studying measures to help its car industry and Fiat which has suffered from a depressed domestic car market saw its shares moved out of negative territory to end up 4.73 percent at 4,485 lire in volumes of nearly 18 million shares.
* The all-share Mibtel index ended up 1.07 percent at 10,415 and the Mib30 1.12 percent firmer at 15,633.

* Fantozzi said intervention was needed in the car industry and the government was studying the problem, but added that no decisions on this matter are imminent. He added this help could be of a fiscal nature or in the form of investment.
* Fiat shares had been depressed early in the day before Fantozzi's comments after it released results for the first nine months of 1996 showing pretax profits down 36 percent.

* Dealers said that trade union satisfactory with the government's Euro-tax also helped market sentiment. This tax is set to raise 12.5 trillion lire, with some 5.5 trillion lire coming from a hike in income tax.

* Olivetti ran out of steam after a strong run over the last few days ending off 0.62 percent at 581 lire, but other De Benedetti stocks faired better, with CIR up 4.95 percent at 903 lire and Cofide 6.17 percent higher at 779.9 lire.
